questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The graph which shows the variation of the de Broglie wavelength ($\lambda$) of a particle and its associated momentum ($p$) is:
questions.explanation: $\lambda = \frac{h}{p} \implies \lambda \propto \frac{1}{p}$, which represents a rectangular hyperbola.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: As the temperature increases, the electrical resistance:
questions.optionA: Increases for both conductors and semiconductors
questions.optionB: Decreases for both conductors and semiconductors
questions.optionC: Increases for conductors but decreases for semiconductors
questions.optionD: Decreases for conductors but increases for semiconductors
questions.explanation: For conductors, resistance increases with temperature due to increased lattice vibrations. For semiconductors, covalent bonds break, increasing charge carriers and decreasing resistance.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Let $T_1$ and $T_2$ be the energy of an electron in the first and second excited states of hydrogen atom, respectively. According to Bohr’s model of an atom, the ratio $T_1 : T_2$ is:
questions.explanation: First excited state corresponds to $n_1 = 2$, second excited state to $n_2 = 3$. Energy $E_n \propto \frac{1}{n^2} \implies \frac{T_1}{T_2} = \frac{n_2^2}{n_1^2} = \frac{3^2}{2^2} = \frac{9}{4}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Two objects of mass $10\text{ kg}$ and $20\text{ kg}$ respectively are connected to the two ends of a rigid rod of length $10\text{ m}$ with negligible mass. The distance of the center of mass of the system from the $10\text{ kg}$ mass is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The ratio of the distance travelled by a freely falling body in the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th second is:
questions.explanation: Galileo’s law of odd numbers: $S_n = u + \frac{a}{2}(2n - 1) \propto (2n - 1) \implies 1 : 3 : 5 : 7$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The ratio of the radius of gyration of a thin uniform disc about an axis passing through its centre and normal to its plane to the radius of gyration about its diameter is:
questions.explanation: $K_1^2 = \frac{R^2}{2} \implies K_1 = \frac{R}{\sqrt{2}}$. $K_2^2 = \frac{R^2}{4} \implies K_2 = \frac{R}{2}$. Ratio $\frac{K_1}{K_2} = \frac{R/\sqrt{2}}{R/2} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{1}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The angular speed of a fly wheel moving with uniform angular acceleration changes from $1200\text{ rpm}$ to $3120\text{ rpm}$ in $16\text{ seconds}$. The angular acceleration in $\text{rad/s}^2$ is:
questions.explanation: $\omega_1 = \frac{1200 \times 2\pi}{60} = 40\pi$, $\omega_2 = \frac{3120 \times 2\pi}{60} = 104\pi$. $\alpha = \frac{\omega_2 - \omega_1}{t} = \frac{104\pi - 40\pi}{16} = 4\pi\text{ rad/s}^2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: An ideal gas undergoes four different processes from the same initial state as shown. The curve which represents the adiabatic process among 1, 2, 3 and 4 is:
questions.explanation: Curve 1 is isochoric, 2 is adiabatic (steeper slope $\gamma P/V$), 3 is isothermal ($P/V$), 4 is isobaric.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Two hollow conducting spheres of radii $R_1$ and $R_2$ ($R_1 \gg R_2$) have equal charges. The potential would be:
questions.explanation: $V = \frac{KQ}{R}$. Since $Q$ is same and $R_1 > R_2$, $V_2 > V_1$ (potential is higher on smaller sphere).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: When light propagates through a material medium of relative permittivity $\varepsilon_r$ and relative permeability $\mu_r$, the velocity of light $v$ is given by ($c = $ velocity in vacuum):
questions.explanation: $v = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\varepsilon \mu}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_0 \mu_0}} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_r \mu_r}} = \frac{c}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_r \mu_r}}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A long solenoid of radius $1\text{ mm}$ has $100\text{ turns per mm}$. If $1\text{ A}$ current flows in the solenoid, the magnetic field strength at the centre is:
questions.explanation: $n = 100/10^{-3} = 10^5\text{ turns/m}$. $B = \mu_0 n I = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 10^5 \times 1 = 4\pi \times 10^{-2} \approx 12.56 \times 10^{-2}\text{ T}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The peak voltage of an ac source is equal to:
questions.optionA: The value of voltage supplied to the circuit
questions.optionB: The rms value of the ac source
questions.optionC: $\sqrt{2}$ times the rms value of the ac source
questions.optionD: $1/\sqrt{2}$ times the rms value of the ac source
questions.explanation: $V_0 = \sqrt{2} V_{\text{rms}}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: An electric lift with a maximum load of $2000\text{ kg}$ (lift + passengers) is moving up with a constant speed of $1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The frictional force opposing motion is $3000\text{ N}$. The minimum power delivered by motor in watts is ($g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$):
questions.explanation: $F = mg + f_{\text{friction}} = 2000(10) + 3000 = 23000\text{ N}$. Power $P = F \cdot v = 23000 \times 1.5 = 34500\text{ W}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: In a Young's double slit experiment, a student observes 8 fringes in a certain segment of screen when monochromatic light of $600\text{ nm}$ is used. If wavelength is changed to $400\text{ nm}$, number of fringes in the same region is:
questions.explanation: $n_1 \lambda_1 = n_2 \lambda_2 \implies 8 \times 600 = n_2 \times 400 \implies n_2 = 12$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A copper wire of length $10\text{ m}$ and radius $(10^{-2}/\sqrt{\pi})\text{ m}$ has electrical resistance of $10\,\Omega$. The current density in the wire for an electric field of $10\text{ V/m}$ is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The dimensions $[\text{MLT}^{-2}\text{A}^{-2}]$ belong to:
questions.explanation: $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r} \implies [\mu_0] = [\text{MLT}^{-2}\text{A}^{-2}]$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: If the initial tension on a stretched string is doubled, then the ratio of initial and final speeds of transverse wave along string is:
questions.explanation: $v = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}} \implies \frac{v_1}{v_2} = \sqrt{\frac{T}{2T}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: In half wave rectification, if the input frequency is $60\text{ Hz}$, then the output ripple frequency would be:
questions.explanation: In half-wave rectifier, output frequency equals input frequency $= 60\text{ Hz}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The displacement-time graphs of two moving particles make angles of $30^\circ$ and $45^\circ$ with the x-axis. The ratio of their velocities is:
questions.explanation: Velocity $= \tan \theta \implies \frac{v_1}{v_2} = \frac{\tan 30^\circ}{\tan 45^\circ} = \frac{1/\sqrt{3}}{1} = 1 : \sqrt{3}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A square loop of side $1\text{ m}$ and resistance $1\,\Omega$ is placed in a magnetic field of $0.5\text{ T}$ perpendicular to the plane of loop. The magnetic flux through the loop is:
questions.explanation: $\Phi = B A \cos 0^\circ = 0.5 \times (1 \times 1) \times 1 = 0.5\text{ Wb}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The energy radiated by a $100\text{ kW}$ transmitter in 1 hour is:
questions.explanation: $E = P \times t = 10^5\text{ W} \times 3600\text{ s} = 36 \times 10^7\text{ J}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A body of mass $60\text{ g}$ experiences a gravitational force of $3.0\text{ N}$, when placed at a particular point. The gravitational field intensity is:
questions.explanation: $E_g = \frac{F}{m} = \frac{3.0}{60 \times 10^{-3}} = 50\text{ N/kg}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText:
Match List-I (Electromagnetic Waves) with List-II (Wavelength):
List-I: (a) AM radio waves, (b) Microwaves, (c) Infrared, (d) X-rays
List-II: (i) $10^{-10}\text{ m}$, (ii) $10^2\text{ m}$, (iii) $10^{-2}\text{ m}$, (iv) $10^{-4}\text{ m}$
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: AM radio $\approx 10^2\text{ m}$ (ii), Microwaves $\approx 10^{-2}\text{ m}$ (iii), Infrared $\approx 10^{-4}\text{ m}$ (iv), X-rays $\approx 10^{-10}\text{ m}$ (i).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A shell of mass $m$ at rest explodes into 3 fragments in ratio $2 : 2 : 1$. If the two equal fragments fly off mutually perpendicular with speed $v$, speed of the lighter fragment is:
questions.explanation: Masses: $0.4m, 0.4m, 0.2m$. Momentum of lighter piece $p_3 = \sqrt{p_1^2 + p_2^2} = \sqrt{2}(0.4mv) = 0.2 m v' \implies v' = 2\sqrt{2}v$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A biconvex lens has radii of curvature $20\text{ cm}$ each. If refractive index $\mu = 1.5$, power of the lens is:
questions.explanation: $\frac{1}{f} = (1.5 - 1)\left(\frac{1}{0.2} - \frac{1}{-0.2}\right) = 0.5 \times 10 = 5\text{ m}^{-1} \implies P = +5\text{ D}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Biot-Savart's law gives the expression for magnetic field of an infinitesimal current element ($I d\vec{l}$).
Statement II: Biot-Savart's law is analogous to Coulomb's law, with the former related to field of a scalar source $I dl$ while latter from vector source $q$.
Choose the correct option:
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.optionC: Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect
questions.optionD: Statement I is incorrect and Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: $I d\vec{l}$ is a vector source and $q$ is a scalar source, making Statement II incorrect.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: In the nuclear reaction: $^{22}_{11}\text{Na} \to \text{X} + e^+ + \nu$, the daughter nucleus $\text{X}$ is:
questions.explanation: Positron emission decreases atomic number $Z$ by 1 while mass number $A$ remains 22: $^{22}_{10}\text{Ne}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Plane angle and solid angle have:
questions.explanation: Plane angle (rad) and solid angle (sr) are supplementary physical quantities having SI units but dimensionless.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The angle between electric lines of force and equipotential surface is:
questions.explanation: Electric field lines are always mutually perpendicular ($90^\circ$) to equipotential surfaces.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A light ray falls on a glass surface of refractive index $\sqrt{3}$ at angle $60^\circ$. The angle between refracted and reflected rays is:
questions.explanation: Brewster's angle: $\tan i_p = \mu = \sqrt{3} \implies i_p = 60^\circ$. At polarizing angle, reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular ($90^\circ$).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: In the given circuits (a), (b) and (c), the potential drop across the two p-n junctions are equal in:
questions.explanation: In both (a) and (c), both diodes are in identical biasing states (either both forward biased or both reverse biased).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A spherical ball is dropped in a long column of highly viscous liquid. The curve representing speed $v(t)$ as a function of time is:
questions.explanation: Viscous drag increases until net force is zero, reaching steady terminal velocity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Two resistors $100\,\Omega$ and $200\,\Omega$ are connected in parallel. The ratio of thermal energy developed in $100\,\Omega$ to $200\,\Omega$ in a given time is:
questions.explanation: In parallel, voltage $V$ is constant: $H = \frac{V^2}{R} t \implies \frac{H_1}{H_2} = \frac{R_2}{R_1} = \frac{200}{100} = 2 : 1$.
