questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: If a soap bubble expands, the excess pressure inside the bubble:
questions.explanation: Excess pressure $\Delta P = \frac{4T}{R}$. As radius $R$ increases, excess pressure $\Delta P$ decreases.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Two point charges $-q$ and $+q$ are placed at distance $L$. The electric field intensity at distance $R$ ($R \gg L$) varies as:
questions.explanation: For an electric dipole, axial and equatorial electric fields vary as $E \propto \frac{1}{R^3}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The area of a rectangular field of length $55.3\text{ m}$ and breadth $25\text{ m}$ after rounding off to correct significant digits is:
questions.explanation: $55.3$ (3 SF) $\times 25$ (2 SF) $= 1382.5\text{ m}^2$. Rounding to 2 significant figures gives $14 \times 10^2\text{ m}^2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: For the given logic circuit (NOT gate on A fed into NAND gate with B), the output C matches truth table:
questions.explanation: Truth table evaluation confirms option (3).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements:
Assertion (A): Stretching of a spring is determined by shear modulus.
Reason (R): Coil spring of copper has more tensile strength than steel spring.
Choose the correct option:
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.optionC: Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect
questions.optionD: Statement I is incorrect and Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Stretching involves twisting of wire (shear modulus). Steel has higher tensile strength than copper.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: From Ampere’s circuital law for a long straight wire of circular cross-section, variation of magnetic field inside and outside is:
questions.optionA: Uniform and constant in both regions
questions.optionB: Linearly increasing inside, linearly decreasing outside
questions.optionC: Linearly increasing function of distance $r$ inside up to boundary, then decreasing with $1/r$ dependence outside
questions.optionD: Linearly decreasing inside, linearly increasing outside
questions.explanation: Inside ($r \le R$): $B \propto r$. Outside ($r > R$): $B \propto 1/r$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A series LCR circuit with $L=10\text{ H}, C=10\,\mu\text{F}, R=50\,\Omega$ is connected to $V=200\sin(100t)\text{ V}$. Resonant frequency $\nu_0$ and ac frequency $\nu$ are:
questions.explanation: $\omega = 100 \implies \nu = \frac{100}{2\pi} = \frac{50}{\pi}\text{ Hz}$. $\nu_0 = \frac{1}{2\pi \sqrt{LC}} = \frac{1}{2\pi \sqrt{10 \times 10^{-5}}} = \frac{50}{\pi}\text{ Hz}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText:
Match List-I with List-II (Gravitational Dimensions):
List-I: (a) Gravitational constant (G), (b) Gravitational potential energy, (c) Gravitational potential, (d) Gravitational intensity
List-II: (i) $[\text{L}^2\text{T}^{-2}]$, (ii) $[\text{M}^{-1}\text{L}^3\text{T}^{-2}]$, (iii) $[\text{LT}^{-2}]$, (iv) $[\text{ML}^2\text{T}^{-2}]$
Choose the correct option:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Two pendulums of length $121\text{ cm}$ and $100\text{ cm}$ start vibrating in phase. Minimum number of vibrations of shorter pendulum to be in phase again is:
questions.explanation: $n_1 T_1 = n_2 T_2 \implies n_1 \sqrt{121} = n_2 \sqrt{100} \implies 11 n_1 = 10 n_2 \implies n_2 = 11$ oscillations.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A circular coil of 1000 turns, radius $10\text{ m}$ rotates at $2\text{ rad/s}$ in Earth's vertical field $2 \times 10^{-5}\text{ T}$. Resistance is $12.56\,\Omega$. Maximum induced current is:
questions.explanation: $\varepsilon_{\max} = N B A \omega = 1000 \times (2 \times 10^{-5}) \times (\pi \cdot 10^2) \times 2 = 4\pi = 12.56\text{ V}$. $I_{\max} = 12.56 / 12.56 = 1\text{ A}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A capacitor $C = 900\text{ pF}$ is charged by $100\text{ V}$ battery, then disconnected and connected to another uncharged $900\text{ pF}$ capacitor. Electrostatic energy stored is:
questions.explanation: $U_{\text{final}} = \frac{Q^2}{2(2C)} = \frac{1}{2} U_{\text{initial}} = \frac{1}{2} \left(\frac{1}{2} C V^2\right) = \frac{1}{4} (900 \times 10^{-12} \times 100^2) = 2.25 \times 10^{-6}\text{ J}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A nucleus of mass number 189 splits into two daughter nuclei of mass numbers 125 and 64. Ratio of their radii $R_1 : R_2$ is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: For the most precise measurement of unknown resistance $X$ using a Wheatstone bridge with variable resistance $Y$, the resistances $P$ and $Q$:
questions.optionB: Should be approximately equal and are small
questions.optionC: Should be very large and unequal
questions.optionD: Do not play any significant role
questions.explanation: Maximum sensitivity and accuracy of a Wheatstone bridge occurs when all four arms have nearly equal, moderate resistances.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The volume occupied by molecules in $4.5\text{ kg}$ water at STP if intermolecular forces vanish is:
questions.explanation: $n = \frac{4500}{18} = 250\text{ moles}$. Volume at STP $= 250 \times 22.4\text{ L} = 5600\text{ L} = 5.6\text{ m}^3$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A ball is projected with velocity $10\text{ m/s}$ at angle $60^\circ$ with vertical. Its speed at highest point is:
questions.explanation: Angle with horizontal $\theta = 90^\circ - 60^\circ = 30^\circ$. At peak, $v_x = u \cos 30^\circ = 10 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 5\sqrt{3}\text{ m/s}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Speeds of light in media A and B are $1.5 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}$ and $2.0 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}$. Critical angle for ray from A to B is:
questions.explanation: $\sin C = \frac{v_A}{v_B} = \frac{1.5 \times 10^8}{2.0 \times 10^8} = 0.750 \implies C = \sin^{-1}(0.750)$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Gadolinium has a low value of third ionisation enthalpy because of:
questions.explanation: $\text{Gd}^{2+}$ ($[\text{Xe}]4f^7 5d^1$) easily loses its $5d^1$ electron to form extra-stable half-filled $4f^7$ configuration.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which one is NOT a correct mathematical equation for Dalton's Law of partial pressure? ($p = $ total pressure):
questions.explanation: $p_i = x_i p_i^\circ$ is Raoult's Law for liquid mixtures, not Dalton's law of partial pressure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements:
Assertion (A): In a point defect, ionic solid is neutral even if few cations are missing.
Reason (R): Frenkel defect arises due to dislocation of cation to interstitial site, maintaining neutrality.
Choose the correct option:
questions.optionA: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.optionB: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.optionC: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.optionD: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are true. Missing cations with neutrality maintenance occurs in Schottky defects or variable valency.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The pH of a buffer solution containing $50\text{ mL}$ each of $0.10\text{ M}$ sodium acetate and $0.01\text{ M}$ acetic acid is (Given $pK_a = 4.57$):
questions.explanation: $\text{pH} = pK_a + \log \frac{[\text{Salt}]}{[\text{Acid}]} = 4.57 + \log \frac{0.10}{0.01} = 4.57 + 1 = 5.57$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Identify the incorrect statement from the following:
questions.optionA: Alkali metals react with water to form hydroxides
questions.optionB: The oxidation number of K in $\text{KO}_2$ is $+4$
questions.optionC: Ionisation enthalpy of alkali metals decreases down the group
questions.optionD: Lithium is the strongest reducing agent in aqueous solution
questions.explanation: In potassium superoxide $\text{KO}_2$, oxidation state of K is $+1$ and superoxide ion is $\text{O}_2^-$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Statement I: Acidic strength of monosubstituted nitrophenol is higher than phenol because of electron withdrawing nitro group.
Statement II: o-, m- and p-nitrophenol will have same acidic strength.
Choose the correct option:
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.optionC: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.optionD: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement I is true. Statement II is false because $-M$ effect operates at ortho/para but only $-I$ operates at meta position.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What mass of $95\%$ pure $\text{CaCO}_3$ is required to neutralise $50\text{ mL}$ of $0.5\text{ M HCl}$?
questions.explanation: Moles of $\text{HCl} = 0.025$. Required pure $\text{CaCO}_3 = 0.0125 \times 100 = 1.25\text{ g}$. Mass of $95\%$ sample $= \frac{1.25}{0.95} = 1.32\text{ g}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The IUPAC name of an element with atomic number 119 is:
questions.explanation: 1 = un, 1 = un, 9 = enn $\implies$ Ununennium (Uue).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Choose the correct statement regarding allotropes of carbon:
questions.optionA: Diamond and graphite have two dimensional network
questions.optionB: Diamond is covalent and graphite is ionic
questions.optionC: Diamond is $sp^3$ hybridised and graphite is $sp^2$ hybridised
questions.optionD: Both diamond and graphite are used as dry lubricants
questions.explanation: In diamond, carbon is $sp^3$ tetrahedral. In graphite, carbon is $sp^2$ in planar hexagonal sheets.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Statement I: In coagulation of negative sol, flocculating power is $\text{Al}^{3+} > \text{Ba}^{2+} > \text{Na}^+$.
Statement II: In coagulation of positive sol, flocculating power is $\text{NaCl} > \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 > \text{Na}_3\text{PO}_4$.
Choose the correct option:
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.optionC: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.optionD: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Hardy-Schulze rule: Higher valency coagulating ion has greater power: $\text{PO}_4^{3-} > \text{SO}_4^{2-} > \text{Cl}^-$ (Statement II reversed).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following p-V curves represents maximum work done during gas expansion?
questions.optionB: Isothermal expansion over wide volume range
questions.explanation: Work done is area under the P-V curve. Complete expansion under isothermal conditions covers maximum area.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Statement I: Primary aliphatic amines react with $\text{HNO}_2$ to give unstable diazonium salts.
Statement II: Primary aromatic amines react with $\text{HNO}_2$ to form diazonium salts which are stable even above $300\text{ K}$.
Choose the correct option:
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.optionC: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.optionD: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Primary aromatic diazonium salts decompose above $278\text{ K}$ ($0-5^\circ\text{C}$).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which amongst the following is an INCORRECT statement?
questions.optionB: $\text{C}_2$ molecule has four electrons in two degenerate $\pi$ molecular orbitals
questions.explanation: $\text{O}_2^+$ has 15 electrons with 1 unpaired electron in $\pi^* 2p$ and is paramagnetic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In the reaction: $\text{RMgX} + \text{CO}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \text{Y} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} \text{RCOOH}$, intermediate Y is:
questions.explanation: Nucleophilic addition of Grignard to $\text{CO}_2$ gives magnesium halocarboxylate adduct $\text{RCOOMgX}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which statement regarding polymers is NOT correct?
questions.optionA: Elastomers have polymer chains held together by weak intermolecular forces
questions.optionC: Thermoplastic polymers repeatedly soften and harden on heating and cooling
questions.explanation: Thermosetting polymers undergo extensive cross-linking on heating and cannot be remoulded or reused.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Given half-cell potentials: $E^\circ_{\text{MnO}_4^-/\text{Mn}^{2+}} = +1.510\text{ V}$ and $E^\circ_{\text{O}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}} = +1.223\text{ V}$. Will $\text{MnO}_4^-$ liberate $\text{O}_2$ from water in presence of acid?
questions.explanation: $E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cathode}} - E^\circ_{\text{anode}} = 1.510 - 1.223 = +0.287\text{ V} > 0$ (spontaneous).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Kjeldahl's method for estimation of nitrogen CANNOT be used for which of the following?
questions.explanation: Kjeldahl method is successful for aniline, but fails for nitro, azo compounds, and nitrogen in ring (pyridine).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The incorrect statement regarding enzymes is:
questions.optionB: Like chemical catalysts enzymes reduce activation energy of bio processes
questions.optionD: Enzymes are very specific for a particular reaction and substrate
questions.explanation: Enzymes are globular proteins, not polysaccharides.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The IUPAC name of the complex $[\text{Ag}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_2][\text{Ag}(\text{CN})_2]$ is:
questions.explanation: Cationic complex: diaquasilver(I). Anionic complex: dicyanidoargentate(I).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List-I with List-II (Drugs):
List-I: (a) Antacids, (b) Antihistamines, (c) Analgesics, (d) Antimicrobials
List-II: (i) Salvarsan, (ii) Morphine, (iii) Cimetidine, (iv) Seldane
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: Antacid = Cimetidine (iii), Antihistamine = Seldane (iv), Analgesic = Morphine (ii), Antimicrobial = Salvarsan (i).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Amongst the following, which one will have MAXIMUM 'lone pair - lone pair' electron repulsions?
questions.explanation: $\text{XeF}_2$ has 3 lone pairs in equatorial positions of trigonal bipyramidal geometry.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Standard electrode potentials: $\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu} = +0.34\text{ V}$, $\text{Zn}^{2+}/\text{Zn} = -0.76\text{ V}$, $\text{Fe}^{2+}/\text{Fe} = -0.44\text{ V}$, $\text{Ag}^+/\text{Ag} = +0.80\text{ V}$. Which reaction CANNOT occur?
questions.explanation: Silver ($+0.80\text{ V}$) is less reactive than copper ($+0.34\text{ V}$) and cannot displace $\text{Cu}^{2+}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Identify the incorrect statement regarding d-orbitals:
questions.optionA: All five 5d orbitals differ in size compared to 4d orbitals
questions.optionB: All five 4d orbitals have shapes similar to 3d orbitals
questions.optionC: All five 3d orbitals are degenerate in free isolated state
questions.optionD: The shapes of $d_{xy}, d_{yz}, d_{zx}$ are similar to each other; and $d_{x^2-y^2}$ and $d_{z^2}$ are similar to each other
questions.explanation: $d_{z^2}$ has a doughnut shape (torus) and is geometrically distinct from four-lobed $d_{x^2-y^2}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In a 1 molal solution containing $0.5\text{ mole}$ of solute, mass of solvent is:
questions.explanation: $\text{Molality} = \frac{\text{moles}}{\text{mass of solvent (kg)}} \implies 1 = \frac{0.5}{W} \implies W = 0.5\text{ kg} = 500\text{ g}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Assertion (A): $\text{ICl}$ is more reactive than $\text{I}_2$.
Reason (R): $\text{I-Cl}$ bond is weaker than $\text{I-I}$ bond.
Choose the correct option:
questions.optionA: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is correct explanation of (A)
questions.optionB: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not correct explanation of (A)
questions.optionC: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.optionD: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: Interhalogen $\text{I-Cl}$ bond is polar and weaker than homonuclear $\text{I-I}$ bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which compound amongst the following is NOT an aromatic compound?
questions.explanation: Cyclooctatetraene adopts a non-planar tub conformation to avoid antiaromaticity and is non-aromatic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Statement I: Boiling points of group 16 hydrides increase in order: $\text{H}_2\text{O} < \text{H}_2\text{S} < \text{H}_2\text{Se} < \text{H}_2\text{Te}$.
Statement II: Boiling points of these hydrides increase with increase in molar mass.
Choose the correct option:
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.optionC: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.optionD: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Due to hydrogen bonding, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ has the highest boiling point: $\text{H}_2\text{S} < \text{H}_2\text{Se} < \text{H}_2\text{Te} < \text{H}_2\text{O}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List-I with List-II (Alkali metals):
List-I: (a) Li, (b) Na, (c) KOH, (d) Cs
List-II: (i) Absorbent for $\text{CO}_2$, (ii) Electrochemical cells, (iii) Coolant in fast breeder reactors, (iv) Photoelectric cell
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: Li = batteries (ii), Na = reactor coolant (iii), KOH = $\text{CO}_2$ scrubber (i), Cs = photoelectric (iv).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following sequence of reactions is suitable to synthesize chlorobenzene?
questions.explanation: Electrophilic aromatic substitution of benzene with $\text{Cl}_2$ in presence of anhydrous $\text{FeCl}_3$ gives chlorobenzene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Statement I: Boiling points of aldehydes and ketones are higher than hydrocarbons of comparable masses due to dipole-dipole interactions.
Statement II: Boiling points of aldehydes and ketones are lower than alcohols of similar masses due to absence of H-bonding.
Choose the correct option:
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.optionC: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.optionD: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct NCERT principles regarding carbonyl physical properties.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Product): (a) Cyanohydrin, (b) Acetal, (c) Schiff’s base, (d) Oxime
List-II (Reagent): (i) $\text{NH}_2\text{OH}$, (ii) $\text{RNH}_2$, (iii) Alcohol, (iv) $\text{HCN}$
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: Cyanohydrin = $\text{HCN}$ (iv), Acetal = Alcohol (iii), Schiff's base = $\text{RNH}_2$ (ii), Oxime = $\text{NH}_2\text{OH}$ (i).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The incorrect statement regarding chirality is:
questions.optionB: $S_N2$ reaction of chiral haloalkane shows inversion of configuration
questions.optionC: Enantiomers are superimposable mirror images on each other
questions.optionD: A racemic mixture shows zero optical rotation
questions.explanation: Enantiomers are non-superimposable mirror images.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List-I with List-II (Hydrides):
List-I: (a) $\text{MgH}_2$, (b) $\text{GeH}_4$, (c) $\text{B}_2\text{H}_6$, (d) $\text{HF}$
List-II: (i) Electron precise, (ii) Electron deficient, (iii) Electron rich, (iv) Ionic
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: $\text{MgH}_2$ = Ionic (iv), $\text{GeH}_4$ = Electron precise (i), $\text{B}_2\text{H}_6$ = Electron deficient (ii), $\text{HF}$ = Electron rich (iii).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about diborane ($\text{B}_2\text{H}_6$)?
questions.optionB: The four terminal B-H bonds are two-centre two-electron bonds
questions.optionC: The four terminal H atoms and two B atoms lie in one plane
questions.explanation: Both boron atoms in diborane are $sp^3$ hybridized.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For a zero order reaction, rate is independent of concentration. For a first order reaction, $t_{1/2}$ is independent of initial concentration. The respective horizontal curves match:
questions.optionA: Zero order ($y = \text{concentration}, x = \text{time}$), First order ($y = t_{1/2}, x = \text{concentration}$)
questions.optionB: Zero order ($y = \text{concentration}, x = \text{time}$), First order ($y = k, x = \text{concentration}$)
questions.optionC: Zero order ($y = \text{rate}, x = \text{concentration}$), First order ($y = t_{1/2}, x = \text{concentration}$)
questions.optionD: Zero order ($y = \text{rate}, x = \text{concentration}$), First order ($y = \text{rate}, x = t_{1/2}$)
questions.explanation: Zero order rate is constant vs concentration; first order half life $t_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{k}$ is constant vs concentration.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List-I with List-II (Ores):
List-I: (a) Haematite, (b) Magnetite, (c) Calamine, (d) Kaolinite
List-II: (i) $\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4$, (ii) $\text{ZnCO}_3$, (iii) $\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$, (iv) $[\text{Al}_2(\text{OH})_4\text{Si}_2\text{O}_5]$
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: Haematite = $\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$ (iii), Magnetite = $\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4$ (i), Calamine = $\text{ZnCO}_3$ (ii), Kaolinite = (iv).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A $10.0\text{ L}$ flask contains $64\text{ g}$ of oxygen at $27^\circ\text{C}$. Pressure in bar is ($R = 0.0831\text{ L bar K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$):
questions.explanation: $n = \frac{64}{32} = 2\text{ moles}$. $P = \frac{nRT}{V} = \frac{2 \times 0.0831 \times 300}{10} = 4.98\text{ bar} \approx 4.95\text{ bar}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For first order reaction $\text{A} \to \text{Products}$, $[\text{A}]_0 = 0.1\text{ M}$ becomes $0.001\text{ M}$ after $5\text{ minutes}$. Rate constant $k$ is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
The order of crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta_o$) and absorbed energy responsible for color among complexes:
(A) $[\text{Ni}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_2(\text{en})_2]^{2+}$, (B) $[\text{Ni}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_4(\text{en})]^{2+}$, (C) $[\text{Ni}(\text{en})_3]^{2+}$ is:
questions.explanation: Ethylenediamine (en) is a stronger ligand than $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Greater number of en ligands increases $\Delta_o$: $C (3\text{ en}) > A (2\text{ en}) > B (1\text{ en})$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For $3\text{O}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{O}_3(g)$, $K_c = 3.0 \times 10^{-59}$ at $298\text{ K}$. If $[\text{O}_2] = 0.040\text{ M}$, equilibrium $[\text{O}_3]$ is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Find EMF of cell: $\text{Ni}(s) + 2\text{Ag}^+(0.001\text{ M}) \to \text{Ni}^{2+}(0.001\text{ M}) + 2\text{Ag}(s)$ (Given $E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 1.05\text{ V}$):

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT formed when acetone reacts with 2-pentanone in presence of dilute $\text{NaOH}$ followed by heating (Cross-aldol)?
questions.explanation: Alcohol derivatives are dehydrated on heating to $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketones; saturated alcohols or 3-propylbut-2-en-1-ol are not formed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The correct IUPAC name of $\text{CH}_2(\text{Br})-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}(\text{Cl})-\text{CH}_3$ is:
questions.explanation: Principal functional group -OH gets lowest locant (position 3 from left). Substituents alphabetized: 1-bromo-5-chloro-4-methylhexan-3-ol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: If radius of second Bohr orbit of $\text{He}^+$ ion is $105.8\text{ pm}$, radius of third Bohr orbit of $\text{Li}^{2+}$ ion is:
questions.explanation: $r \propto \frac{n^2}{Z} \implies \frac{r_2}{r_1} = \frac{3^2 / 3}{2^2 / 2} = \frac{3}{2} \implies r_2 = 1.5 \times 105.8 = 158.7\text{ pm}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compound X on ozonolysis followed by $\text{Zn}/\text{H}_2\text{O}$ gives formaldehyde and 2-methylpropanal. Compound X is:
questions.explanation: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{O}_3 \to \text{HCHO} + (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCHO}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In neutral or faintly alkaline medium, $\text{KMnO}_4$ oxidises iodide into iodate. Change in oxidation state of Mn is:
questions.explanation: In alkaline medium: $2\text{MnO}_4^- (+7) + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{I}^- \to 2\text{MnO}_2 (+4) + 2\text{OH}^- + \text{IO}_3^-$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Pollution due to oxides of sulphur gets enhanced due to presence of:
(a) Particulate matter, (b) Ozone, (c) Hydrocarbons, (d) Hydrogen peroxide.
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: Oxidation of $\text{SO}_2$ to $\text{SO}_3$ is catalyzed by particulate matter, ozone, and $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Statement I: In Lucas test, primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols are distinguished with conc $\text{HCl} + \text{ZnCl}_2$.
Statement II: Primary alcohols immediately produce turbidity at room temperature.
Choose the correct option:
questions.optionA: Both statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.optionB: Both statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.optionC: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.optionD: Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
questions.explanation: $3^\circ$ alcohols produce turbidity immediately; $1^\circ$ alcohols do not produce turbidity at room temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Copper crystallises in fcc with edge length $3.608 \times 10^{-8}\text{ cm}$ and density $8.92\text{ g/cm}^3$. Atomic mass of copper is:
questions.explanation: $M = \frac{d \cdot N_A \cdot a^3}{Z} = \frac{8.92 \times (6.022 \times 10^{23}) \times (3.608 \times 10^{-8})^3}{4} \approx 63.1\text{ u}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Product formed in sequence: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CN} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} \xrightarrow{\text{NaNO}_2+\text{HCl}} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O}} \text{Product}$ is:
questions.explanation: Reduction of benzonitrile gives benzylamine ($\text{PhCH}_2\text{NH}_2$). Diazotization of primary aliphatic amine followed by hydrolysis yields benzyl alcohol.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements:
Assertion (A): Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is used in DNA amplification.
Reason (R): Ampicillin resistant gene is used as selectable marker to check transformation.
Choose the correct option:
questions.optionA: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is correct explanation of (A)
questions.optionB: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not correct explanation of (A)
questions.optionC: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.optionD: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are true. PCR amplifies DNA in vitro, while antibiotic markers check transformation in cloning.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The process of translation of mRNA to proteins begins as soon as:
questions.optionA: The small subunit of ribosome encounters mRNA
questions.optionB: The larger subunit of ribosome encounters mRNA
questions.optionC: Both subunits join together to bind with mRNA
questions.optionD: tRNA is activated and larger subunit encounters mRNA
questions.explanation: Translation initiates when the small 40S/30S ribosomal subunit binds to mRNA at the ribosome binding site.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The gaseous plant growth regulator (Ethylene) is used in plants to:
questions.optionB: Promote root growth and root hair formation to increase absorption surface
questions.explanation: Ethylene promotes root growth and root hair formation, significantly increasing surface area for water absorption.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Exoskeleton of arthropods is composed of:
questions.explanation: Arthropod exoskeleton is made of chitin, a complex nitrogenous polysaccharide.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT observed during an apoplastic pathway?
questions.optionA: Movement of water occurs through intercellular spaces and cell walls
questions.optionB: The movement does not involve crossing of cell membrane
questions.optionC: The movement is aided by cytoplasmic streaming
questions.optionD: Apoplast is continuous and does not provide barrier to water
questions.explanation: Cytoplasmic streaming aids symplastic transport across living cytoplasm, not apoplastic transport.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a method of ex situ conservation?
questions.explanation: National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries, and Biosphere Reserves are in situ (on-site) conservation methods.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match List-I with List-II (Plant Nutrients):
List-I: (a) Manganese, (b) Magnesium, (c) Boron, (d) Iron
List-II: (i) Activates catalase, (ii) Pollen germination, (iii) Respiration enzymes, (iv) Photolysis of water
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: Mn = photolysis (iv), Mg = respiration/photosynthesis (iii), Boron = pollen germination (ii), Fe = catalase (i).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is NOT true regarding gel electrophoresis?
questions.optionA: Extraction of separated DNA strands from gel is elution
questions.optionB: Separated DNA fragments are stained with ethidium bromide
questions.optionC: Presence of chromogenic substrate gives blue coloured DNA bands on gel
questions.optionD: Bright orange bands of DNA are observed under UV light
questions.explanation: DNA in agarose gel is visualized by EtBr fluorescence under UV light as bright orange bands (no chromogenic blue bands).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT true regarding chemiosmotic ATP synthesis in chloroplasts?
questions.optionC: Movement of protons across membrane to stroma
questions.optionD: Reduction of NADP to $\text{NADPH}_2$ on stroma side
questions.explanation: ATP synthesis is driven by a proton gradient ($Delta\text{pH}$ and potential), not an electron gradient.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: DNA polymorphism forms the basis of:
questions.optionC: Both genetic mapping and DNA fingerprinting
questions.explanation: Polymorphism in DNA sequences (VNTRs, satellite DNA) forms the basis of genetic linkage mapping and DNA fingerprinting.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Habitat loss, over-exploitation, alien species invasion and co-extinction ('The Evil Quartet') are causes for:
questions.explanation: 'The Evil Quartet' describes four major human-induced causes of accelerating biodiversity loss.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The device which removes $>99\%$ of particulate matter present in exhaust from thermal power plants is:
questions.explanation: Electrostatic precipitators charge and collect airborne particulate matter efficiently.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which one of the following plants does NOT show plasticity (heterophylly)?
questions.explanation: Cotton, coriander, larkspur, and buttercup show developmental/environmental plasticity; maize does not.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements CANNOT be connected to Predation?
questions.optionA: It helps in maintaining species diversity in community
questions.optionB: It might lead to extinction of species if predator is over-efficient
questions.optionC: Both interacting species are negatively impacted
questions.optionD: It is necessitated by nature to transfer energy across trophic levels
questions.explanation: Predation is a $(+,-)$ interaction where predator benefits and prey is harmed (not $(-,-)$ like competition).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: What amount of energy is released from glucose during lactic acid fermentation?
questions.explanation: Anaerobic fermentation releases less than $7\%$ of total energy trapped in glucose.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Mendel studied seven pairs of contrasting traits in pea plants and proposed Laws of Inheritance.
Statement II: Seven characters examined were seed shape/colour, flower colour/position, pod shape/colour, and stem height.
Choose the correct option:
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.optionC: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.optionD: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements accurately detail Mendel's foundational 7 traits in Pisum sativum.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Statement I: Decomposition degrades detritus into simpler substances by microbes.
Statement II: Decomposition is faster if detritus is rich in lignin and chitin.
Choose the correct option:
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.optionC: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.optionD: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Decomposition is slower if detritus is rich in lignin and chitin, and faster if rich in nitrogen and sugars.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Choose the set of correct statements regarding chromatin:
(a) Euchromatin is loosely packed chromatin
(b) Heterochromatin is transcriptionally active
(c) Histone octamer is wrapped by negatively charged DNA
(d) Histones are rich in lysine and arginine
(e) A typical nucleosome contains 400 bp of DNA
Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation: (a), (c), (d) are true. Heterochromatin is inactive (b is false), nucleosome contains 200 bp (e is false).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following plants shows vexillary aestivation and diadelphous stamens?
questions.explanation: Pisum sativum (Fabaceae) shows butterfly-like vexillary aestivation and $(9)+1$ diadelphous stamens.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
In old trees, greater part of secondary xylem is dark brown and durable due to:
(a) Secretion of secondary metabolites in vessel lumens
(b) Deposition of tannins and resins in central heartwood
(c) Deposition of suberin in outer bark
(d) Peripheral sapwood deposition
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: Heartwood (duramen) is non-functional, durable, and dark due to central deposition of tannins, resins, and gums.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Read the statements about vascular bundles:
(a) Radial bundles have xylem and phloem on alternate radii
(b) Conjoint closed bundles lack cambium
(c) Open bundles have cambium between xylem and phloem
(d) Dicot stem bundles possess endarch protoxylem
(e) Monocot roots have polyarch bundles (>6 xylem groups)
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: All statements (a, b, c, d, e) are correct botanical facts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which one of the following NEVER occurs during mitotic cell division?
questions.optionB: Movement of centrioles to opposite poles
questions.explanation: Synapsis and crossing over occur exclusively during Meiosis I (Zygotene/Pachytene), never in mitosis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Application of which phytohormone increases yield in cucumber by promoting female flowers (femaleness)?
questions.explanation: Ethylene promotes femaleness in cucumber and pineapple.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The flowers are zygomorphic (bilaterally symmetrical) in:
questions.explanation: Gulmohar, Cassia, and Pea have zygomorphic flowers. Mustard, Datura, and Chilli are actinomorphic.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Identify the correct set of plant modifications:
(a) Leaflets modified into thorns in Citrus
(b) Axillary buds form tendrils in cucumber and pumpkin
(c) Flattened photosynthetic stems in Opuntia
(d) Pneumatophores in Rhizophora
(e) Runners in grass and strawberry
Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation: Thorns in Citrus are modified axillary buds (stems), not leaflets. Statements (b), (c), (d), (e) are correct.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is INCORRECTLY matched with its stored reserve food?
questions.explanation: Ulothrix is a green alga (Chlorophyceae) that stores starch, not mannitol (which is stored by brown algae).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which organism produces nitrogen-fixing root nodules on non-leguminous Alnus trees?
questions.explanation: Frankia forms symbiotic nitrogen-fixing nodules on the roots of non-leguminous plants like Alnus and Casuarina.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Identify the INCORRECT statement related to Pollination:
questions.optionA: Pollination by water is quite rare in flowering plants
questions.optionB: Pollination by wind is more common amongst abiotic pollination
questions.optionC: Flowers produce foul odours to attract flies and beetles
questions.optionD: Moths and butterflies are the most dominant pollinating agents among insects
questions.explanation: Bees are the most dominant and common insect pollinating agents.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Statement I: Cleistogamous flowers are invariably autogamous.
Statement II: Cleistogamy is disadvantageous as there is no chance for cross-pollination.
Choose the correct option:
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.optionC: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.optionD: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Cleistogamous flowers do not open, guaranteeing autogamy but eliminating genetic variability.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Hydrocolloid Carrageen is commercially obtained from:
questions.explanation: Carrageen is obtained from red algae (Rhodophyceae), whereas algin is obtained from brown algae (Phaeophyceae).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: What is the net gain of ATP when one molecule of glucose is converted to two molecules of pyruvic acid in glycolysis?
questions.explanation: Total 4 ATP generated - 2 ATP consumed in preparatory phase $= 2\text{ ATP}$ net gain.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Appearance of recombination nodules on homologous chromosomes during meiosis characterizes:
questions.optionC: Sites at which crossing over occurs
questions.explanation: Recombination nodules are protein complexes marking sites where non-sister chromatids cross over in Pachytene.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Statement I: The primary $\text{CO}_2$ acceptor in $\text{C}_4$ plants is phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) in mesophyll cells.
Statement II: Mesophyll cells of $\text{C}_4$ plants lack RuBisCO enzyme.
Choose the correct option:
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.optionC: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.optionD: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: In $\text{C}_4$ plants, PEP carboxylase is in mesophyll and RuBisCO is confined to bundle sheath cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The 'Girdling Experiment' was performed by plant physiologists to identify transport of:
questions.explanation: Removing bark ring (phloem) causes food accumulation above the girdle, demonstrating phloem translocates organic nutrients.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: XO type of chromosomal sex determination is found in:
questions.explanation: In grasshoppers, males have only one X chromosome (XO) and females have two (XX).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Addition of more solutes to a given solution will:
questions.optionB: Lower its water potential (make it more negative)
questions.explanation: Pure water has maximum water potential ($Psi_w = 0$). Adding solutes lowers $Psi_w$ to negative values.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The blind approach of sequencing both coding and non-coding parts of the genome in HGP is known as:
questions.explanation: Sequence Annotation involves sequencing whole genome and assigning functional annotations later.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is an autosome-linked dominant genetic disorder?
questions.explanation: Myotonic dystrophy is autosomal dominant. Sickle cell and thalassemia are autosomal recessive; haemophilia is X-linked recessive.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Assertion (A): Mendel’s law of Independent Assortment does not hold good for closely located genes.
Reason (R): Closely located genes assort independently.
Choose the correct option:
questions.optionA: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is correct explanation of (A)
questions.optionB: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not correct explanation of (A)
questions.optionC: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.optionD: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: Linked genes do not assort independently because they are physically linked on the same chromosome.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which part of the fruit makes an apple a false fruit?
questions.explanation: In apple and pear, the edible fleshy part develops from the floral thalamus rather than ovary wall alone.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Read the statements on lipids:
(a) Lecithin is a phospholipid
(b) Saturated fatty acids lack carbon-carbon double bonds
(c) Gingelly oil has low melting point and remains liquid in winter
(d) Lipids are insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents
(e) Fatty acids esterified with glycerol form glycerides
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: Statements (a), (c), (d), (e) are correct NCERT lipid properties.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Transposons (jumping genes) can be utilized during:
questions.explanation: Transposons are mobile genetic elements used in gene sequencing and insertional mutagenesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which interspecific interaction is assigned $(+)$ for one species and $(-)$ for another?
questions.explanation: Predation and parasitism are $(+,-)$ interactions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In the palindromic sequences of DNA, which one is the recognition site of EcoRI?
questions.explanation: EcoRI recognizes hexanucleotide palindrome $5'\text{-GAATTC-3'}$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which one of the following will accelerate the sedimentary phosphorus cycle in nature?
questions.explanation: Natural reservoir of phosphorus is rocks; weathering releases mineral phosphates into soil solution.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Regarding conversion of public buses in Delhi to CNG from diesel, which statement is FALSE?
questions.optionA: CNG burns more efficiently than diesel
questions.optionB: The same diesel engine is used in CNG buses making conversion cost low
questions.optionD: CNG cannot be easily siphoned or adulterated
questions.explanation: Dedicated CNG engines must replace diesel engines; existing diesel engines cannot simply be used without modification.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match plant with life cycle:
(a) Spirogyra, (b) Fern, (c) Funaria, (d) Cycas
(i) Diplontic with reduced gametophyte, (ii) Haplontic with dominant free gametophyte, (iii) Haplo-diplontic (sporophyte dominant with prothallus), (iv) Haplo-diplontic (gametophyte dominant)
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: Spirogyra = Haplontic (ii), Fern = Haplo-diplontic sporophyte (iii), Moss/Funaria = Gametophyte dominant (iv), Cycas = Diplontic (i).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match chromosome types:
(a) Metacentric, (b) Acrocentric, (c) Sub-metacentric, (d) Telocentric
(i) Centromere close to end (one very short arm), (ii) Terminal centromere, (iii) Middle centromere (equal arms), (iv) Slightly off-center (one shorter arm)
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: Metacentric = Middle (iii), Acrocentric = Sub-terminal (i), Sub-metacentric = Slightly off-center (iv), Telocentric = Terminal (ii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Identify the correct statements about springwood:
(a) Also called early wood
(b) Cambium produces wide cavity vessels
(c) Lighter in colour
(d) Forms annual ring with autumnwood
(e) Has lower density
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: All statements regarding springwood/early wood are correct NCERT anatomical facts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The role of large Kranz bundle sheath cells around vascular bundles in $\text{C}_4$ plants is:
questions.optionA: To provide site of photorespiratory pathway
questions.optionB: To provide high number of chloroplasts for Calvin cycle operation
questions.optionC: To enable plant to tolerate high temperature
questions.optionD: To protect vascular tissues from light
questions.explanation: Bundle sheath cells contain numerous agranal chloroplasts rich in RuBisCO to operate Calvin cycle without photorespiration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Statement I: Fatty acids and glycerol cannot be absorbed directly into blood.
Statement II: Lymphatic lacteals carry chylomicrons into lymphatic vessels and blood.
Choose the correct option:
questions.optionA: Both statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.optionB: Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
questions.optionC: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
questions.optionD: Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Insoluble fats form micelles and chylomicrons transported through intestinal lacteals into circulation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Statement I: Release of sperms into seminiferous tubules lumen is spermiation.
Statement II: Transformation of spermatids into spermatozoa is spermiogenesis.
Choose the correct option:
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.optionC: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.optionD: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Spermiogenesis transforms spermatids into sperms; spermiation releases them from Sertoli cells into lumen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a function of conducting part of respiratory tract?
questions.optionA: Clears inhaled air from foreign particles
questions.optionD: Provides actual surface for diffusion of $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$
questions.explanation: Alveoli and alveolar ducts form the respiratory/exchange part where gas diffusion occurs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The fungus responsible for industrial production of immunosuppressant Cyclosporin A is:
questions.explanation: Trichoderma polysporum produces Cyclosporin A used in organ transplantation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Under normal physiological conditions, every $100\text{ mL}$ of oxygenated blood delivers _______ of $\text{O}_2$ to tissues.
questions.explanation: Every $100\text{ mL}$ of oxygenated blood carries $20\text{ mL}$ and delivers $5\text{ mL}$ of $\text{O}_2$ under resting conditions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Tegmina (forewings) in cockroach arise from:
questions.explanation: First pair of opaque leathery forewings (tegmina) arise from mesothorax.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In situ conservation refers to:
questions.optionA: Protecting and conserving species in their whole natural ecosystem
questions.optionC: Conserving only endangered species in zoos
questions.explanation: In situ conservation protects endangered flora and fauna within their natural habitats and ecosystems.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Detritivores break down dead detritus into smaller fragments. This process is called:
questions.explanation: Physical breakdown of detritus into smaller particles by earthworms/detritivores is fragmentation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: When two glucose molecules ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6$) condense via dehydration synthesis, chemical formula of maltose is:
questions.explanation: $2 \times \text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6 - \text{H}_2\text{O} = \text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11}$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Identify the asexual reproductive spore structure associated with Penicillium:
questions.explanation: Penicillium produces non-motile exogenous asexual spores called conidia on conidiophores.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Select the INCORRECT statement with reference to Mitosis:
questions.optionA: All chromosomes lie at equator at metaphase
questions.optionB: Spindle fibres attach to centromere of chromosomes
questions.optionD: Splitting of centromere occurs at anaphase
questions.explanation: Spindle fibres attach to disc-shaped kinetochores on centromeres (not directly to centromeric DNA).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements with respect to Endoplasmic Reticulum is INCORRECT?
questions.optionA: RER has ribosomes attached to outer surface
questions.optionC: In prokaryotes only RER are present
questions.optionD: SER are major sites for lipid and steroid synthesis
questions.explanation: Prokaryotes lack all membrane-bound organelles including ER.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In taxonomic categories, which hierarchical arrangement in descending order is correct for animals?
questions.optionA: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
questions.optionB: Kingdom, Class, Phylum, Family, Order, Genus, Species
questions.optionC: Kingdom, Order, Class, Phylum, Family, Genus, Species
questions.optionD: Kingdom, Order, Phylum, Class, Family, Genus, Species
questions.explanation: Correct taxonomic hierarchy: Kingdom $\to$ Phylum $\to$ Class $\to$ Order $\to$ Family $\to$ Genus $\to$ Species.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In which animals does the digestive tract have additional muscular chambers like crop and gizzard?
questions.explanation: Birds (Aves) and insects possess crop for food storage and gizzard for mastication.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Statement I: Mycoplasma can pass through less than $1\,\mu\text{m}$ filter size.
Statement II: Mycoplasma are bacteria with a rigid cell wall.
Choose the correct option:
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.optionC: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.optionD: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Mycoplasma ($0.3\,\mu\text{m}$) completely lack a cell wall (Statement II false).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a connective tissue?
questions.explanation: Neuroglia are supporting cells of nervous tissue, not connective tissue.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Nitrogenous waste is excreted in the form of dry pellet or paste (uricotelic) by:
questions.explanation: Birds (Pavo), reptiles, insects, and land snails excrete uric acid as pellet/paste to conserve water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Assertion (A): All vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrates.
Reason (R): Notochord is replaced by vertebral column in adult vertebrates.
Choose the correct option:
questions.optionA: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is correct explanation of (A)
questions.optionB: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not correct explanation of (A)
questions.optionC: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.optionD: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: Vertebrates possess notochord in embryonic stages, which is replaced by cartilaginous/bony vertebral column in adults.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is a CORRECT match for disease and its primary cause/symptom?
questions.optionC: Myasthenia gravis - Genetic disorder of skeletal muscle
questions.optionD: Muscular dystrophy - Autoimmune destruction of neuromuscular junction
questions.explanation: Arthritis is joint inflammation. Tetany is due to low calcium (hypocalcemia). Myasthenia gravis is autoimmune; muscular dystrophy is genetic.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Assertion (A): Osteoporosis is characterised by decreased bone mass and increased fracture risk.
Reason (R): Common cause of osteoporosis in post-menopausal women is increased levels of estrogen.
Choose the correct option:
questions.optionA: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is correct explanation of (A)
questions.optionB: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not correct explanation of (A)
questions.optionC: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.optionD: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: Osteoporosis in post-menopausal women is caused by deficiency / decreased estrogen levels (Reason is false).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In an E. coli strain, the $i$ gene is mutated so its repressor cannot bind the inducer (lactose). If lactose is added, the outcome will be:
questions.optionA: Only z gene will get transcribed
questions.optionB: z, y, a genes will be transcribed
questions.optionC: z, y, a structural genes will NOT be transcribed/translated
questions.optionD: RNA polymerase will bind the promoter region
questions.explanation: The repressor remains permanently bound to the operator, preventing transcription of structural genes (lac operon stays OFF).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: If the length of a double helix DNA molecule is $1.1\text{ metres}$, what will be the approximate number of base pairs ($0.34\text{ nm}$ per bp)?
questions.explanation: Number of $\text{bp} = \frac{1.1\text{ m}}{0.34 \times 10^{-9}\text{ m}} = 3.24 \times 10^9 \approx 3.3 \times 10^9\text{ bp}$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Which statements are true for Spermatogenesis but do NOT hold true for Oogenesis?
(a) Results in formation of haploid gametes
(b) Differentiation occurs after completion of meiosis
(c) Meiosis occurs continuously in stem cell population
(d) Controlled by LH and FSH
(e) Initiated at puberty
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: Spermatogenesis starts at puberty and is continuous (c, e). Oogenesis begins during embryonic development and is discontinuous.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is present between adjacent vertebrae in the vertebral column to allow limited movement?
questions.explanation: Cartilaginous joints with intervertebral fibrocartilaginous discs connect adjacent vertebrae.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Regarding Meiosis, which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
questions.optionA: There are two sequential cycles of nuclear and cell division: Meiosis I and II
questions.optionB: DNA replication occurs in S phase of Meiosis-II
questions.optionC: Pairing of homologous chromosomes and recombination occurs in Meiosis-I
questions.optionD: Four haploid cells are formed at the end of Meiosis-II
questions.explanation: DNA replication occurs only once during interphase S-phase prior to Meiosis I (no DNA replication before Meiosis II).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Statement I: Autoimmune disorder is a condition where body defense recognizes self cells as foreign.
Statement II: Rheumatoid arthritis is a condition where body does not attack self cells.
Choose the correct option:
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.optionC: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.optionD: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune disorder where antibodies attack self joint tissues.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Natural selection where more individuals acquire a specific character value other than the mean peak value leads to:
questions.explanation: Directional selection shifts the peak of phenotypic distribution towards one specific direction.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Statement I: Blood coagulum is formed of a network of threads called thrombins.
Statement II: Spleen is the graveyard of erythrocytes (RBCs).
Choose the correct option:
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.optionC: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.optionD: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Blood clot is formed of fibrin mesh (not thrombin). Spleen destroys aging 120-day RBCs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Breeding crops with higher levels of vitamins, minerals, proteins, and healthy fats is called:
questions.explanation: Biofortification improves the nutritional quality of staple crops through breeding and biotechnology (e.g. Golden Rice).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In gene therapy of ADA deficiency, patient requires periodic infusion of engineered lymphocytes because:
questions.optionA: Retroviral vector is introduced into these lymphocytes
questions.optionB: Gene isolated from marrow is introduced at embryonic stage
questions.optionC: Lymphocytes are grown in culture outside body
questions.optionD: Genetically engineered mature lymphocytes are not immortal and have finite life span
questions.explanation: Mature somatic lymphocytes have finite life spans, requiring repeated infusions unless performed on embryonic stem cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: At which stage of human female life is the oogenesis process initiated?
questions.explanation: Oogenesis is initiated during embryonic development when millions of oogonia are formed in fetal ovaries.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Lippes loop is a type of contraceptive used as a:
questions.explanation: Lippes loop is a classical non-medicated plastic double-S shaped intrauterine device.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following digestive functions is NOT performed by secretions of salivary glands?
questions.optionB: Digestion of complex starches via ptyalin
questions.optionC: Lubrication of oral cavity via mucin
questions.explanation: Disaccharidases (maltase, sucrase, lactase) are secreted in succus entericus of small intestine, not in saliva.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: If 8 Drosophila in a laboratory population of 80 died during a week, the death rate is:
questions.explanation: $\text{Death rate} = \frac{8}{80} = 0.1\text{ individuals per Drosophila per week}$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Statement I: Restriction endonucleases recognize specific palindromic nucleotide sequences.
Statement II: Restriction endonucleases cut DNA strands a little away from the centre of the palindromic site.
Choose the correct option:
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.optionC: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.optionD: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are true. Type II restriction enzymes produce single-stranded sticky ends by cutting staggered bonds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is a CORRECT statement?
questions.optionA: Cyanobacteria are autotrophic photosynthetic organisms classified under Kingdom Monera
questions.optionC: Slime moulds are saprophytes classified under Kingdom Monera
questions.optionD: Mycoplasma have DNA, Ribosome and cell wall
questions.explanation: Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) are photosynthetic prokaryotes belonging to Kingdom Monera.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which statement is correct about genetically engineered Human Insulin (Humulin)?
questions.optionB: A and B peptide chains were produced separately in E. coli, extracted and combined via disulfide bonds
questions.optionC: Insulin used was extracted from pancreas of slaughtered cattle
questions.optionD: Pro-hormone needs cleavage of C-peptide in vitro
questions.explanation: Eli Lilly produced separate A and B chains in E. coli and combined them chemically with disulfide linkages.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Statement I: In a scrubber, exhaust is passed through electric wires to charge dust particles.
Statement II: Fine particulate matter (PM 2.5) cannot be removed by scrubbers but can be removed by ESPs.
Choose the correct option:
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.optionC: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.optionD: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Scrubbers spray water/lime (not electric wires), and neither standard ESP nor scrubber easily captures PM 2.5.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Recombination frequencies: a-c = $5\%$, b-c = $15\%$, b-d = $9\%$, a-b = $20\%$, c-d = $24\%$, a-d = $29\%$. The linear gene sequence is:
questions.explanation: $a \xrightarrow{5\text{ cM}} c \xrightarrow{15\text{ cM}} b \xrightarrow{9\text{ cM}} d$. Total $a-d = 5 + 15 + 9 = 29\text{ cM}$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match List-I with List-II (Biomolecules):
List-I: (a) Glycogen, (b) Globulin, (c) Steroids, (d) Thrombin
List-II: (i) Hormone / lipid, (ii) Biocatalyst / enzyme, (iii) Defense antibody, (iv) Storage carbohydrate
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: Glycogen = Storage (iv), Globulin = Antibody (iii), Steroids = Hormone (i), Thrombin = Enzyme (ii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match contraceptive methods with actions:
(a) Diaphragms, (b) Oral Pills, (c) IUDs, (d) Lactational Amenorrhea
(i) Inhibit ovulation and implantation, (ii) Increase sperm phagocytosis in uterus, (iii) Absence of menstrual cycle during lactation, (iv) Cover cervix blocking sperm entry
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: Diaphragm = Barrier (iv), Oral pills = Inhibit ovulation (i), IUDs = Phagocytosis (ii), Lactational Amenorrhea = (iii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are NOT direct physiological effects of Parathyroid Hormone (PTH)?
(a) Stimulates bone resorption
(b) Decreases $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ level in blood
(c) Stimulates renal $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ reabsorption
(d) Decreases absorption of $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ from intestine
(e) Increases carbohydrate metabolism
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: PTH is hypercalcemic (increases blood calcium) and stimulates bone resorption and intestinal calcium absorption.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Select the INCORRECT statement with respect to acquired immunity:
questions.optionA: Primary response is produced upon first encounter with pathogen
questions.optionB: Anamnestic response is elicited on subsequent encounters with same pathogen
questions.optionC: Anamnestic response is due to immunological memory
questions.optionD: Acquired immunity is a non-specific defense present at time of birth
questions.explanation: Innate immunity is non-specific and present at birth; acquired immunity is pathogen-specific and adaptive.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Ten E. coli cells with $^{15}\text{N}$-dsDNA divide in $^{14}\text{N}$ medium for $60\text{ minutes}$ (3 generations). How many cells have DNA totally free from $^{15}\text{N}$?
questions.explanation: After 3 rounds (80 total cells), 20 cells contain hybrid $^{15}\text{N}-^{14}\text{N}$ DNA and 60 cells contain completely light $^{14}\text{N}-^{14}\text{N}$ DNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: If a colour blind female ($X^c X^c$) marries a man whose mother was colour blind ($X^c Y$), what percentage of their progeny will be colour blind?
questions.explanation: All sons ($X^c Y$) and all daughters ($X^c X^c$) inherit mutated $X^c$ chromosomes $\implies 100\%$ colour blind.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a desirable feature of a cloning vector?
questions.optionC: Presence of single unique restriction enzyme site
questions.optionD: Presence of two or more recognition sites for the same restriction enzyme
questions.explanation: Multiple recognition sites for a single restriction enzyme would cut the vector into multiple fragments, complicating cloning.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match List-I with List-II (Tissues):
List-I: (a) Bronchioles, (b) Goblet cells, (c) Tendons, (d) Adipose tissue
List-II: (i) Dense regular connective tissue, (ii) Loose connective tissue, (iii) Glandular epithelium, (iv) Ciliated epithelium
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: Bronchioles = Ciliated (iv), Goblet cells = Glandular (iii), Tendons = Dense regular (i), Adipose = Loose connective (ii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is CORRECT regarding the cardiac cycle?
questions.optionA: AVN generates action potential to stimulate atrial contraction
questions.optionB: Tricuspid and bicuspid valves open due to pressure of atrial contraction
questions.optionC: Blood moves freely from atria to ventricles during joint diastole
questions.optionD: Increased ventricular pressure causes closing of semilunar valves
questions.explanation: During joint diastole, AV valves are open and about $70\%$ of blood flows passively from atria into relaxed ventricles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Select the INCORRECT statement regarding synapses:
questions.optionA: Presynaptic and postsynaptic membranes are in close proximity in electrical synapses
questions.optionB: Electrical current flows directly from one neuron to next across electrical synapse
questions.optionD: Impulse transmission across chemical synapse is always faster than electrical synapse
questions.explanation: Transmission across electrical synapses (gap junctions) is virtually instantaneous and faster than chemical synapses.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is NOT true regarding evolutionary biology?
questions.optionA: Analogous structures are a result of convergent evolution
questions.optionB: Sweet potato (root) and potato (stem) is an example of analogy
questions.optionC: Homology indicates common ancestry and divergent evolution
questions.optionD: Flippers of penguins and dolphins are a pair of homologous organs
questions.explanation: Flippers of penguins (birds) and dolphins (mammals) are analogous structures that evolved convergently for aquatic locomotion.
